messages:
Maria T.: Quick heads-up — APAC canary for routing-policy v2 showed a p99 jump (~+140ms) around 03:10 UTC after we enabled the new fallback rule. p50 looks unchanged. Observed: requests fail over across regions, kernel selection falls back to older compat path, and KV cache thrash increases. cc @Kevin L. @Anita P.

Kevin L.: Can you paste the tail logs and any profiler traces? Is this KV miss amplification or pure kernel throughput drop?

Maria T.: Logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T03:10:12Z [router] route=ap-northeast -> fallback=us-west
2026-03-17T03:10:12Z [serve] kernel=quant-int8-compat
2026-03-17T03:10:12Z [cache] kv_miss_rate=0.42 evictions/s=120
2026-03-17T03:10:13Z [latency] p99=460ms (+140ms)
```

Anita P.: Looks like a kernel mismatch forced the slower compat kernel on fallback nodes. That kernel has worse per-token overhead at short sequences. Also when routing flips we lose shard affinity so KV misses spike. Microbatching behavior matters here — if we revert to single-request fast-path the per-token penalty is proportionally larger.

Jeff R.: Did the canary use identical microbatch settings across regions? APAC traffic tends to have short prompts — swap penalty bigger for seq<=64.

Maria T.: Canary used adaptive microbatching. But when the route changed, the batcher couldn't merge requests (region tag mismatch) so requests take the singleton path. That exposes kernel startup/compat overhead and increases KV eviction rate.

oncall-sre: FYI we saw a similar pattern in EU last week (INC-2219). Rolling back the routing policy reduced p99. We should avoid ad-hoc cross-region fallback that breaks affinity.

Kevin L.: Proposed next steps:
- Add kernel-capability hints to routing so fallback prefers nodes with compatible kernels (cheap win).
- Keep KV shard affinity across soft fallbacks where possible (sticky keys / short-term reroute).
- Add a guardrail: do NOT cross-region-fallback for requests with seq<64 unless capacity emergency.

Anita P.: Also want a quick perf sweep: run latency profiles for seq=32/64/128 on kernels `quant-int8-compat` vs `opt-kernel-v2` with microbatch sizes 1/4/8 to quantify tail. I can generate a small matrix job in staging.

Maria T.: I'll kick off the sweep and attach p95/p99 deltas. FYI user-facing SLO is 250ms p99; when fallback triggered we hit ~460ms.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollback performed for routing-policy v2 (rollout id r-2026-47) — done :white_check_mark:

Kevin L.: Once sweep is in, sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. I'll draft the fallback policy change and an experiment plan.

Maria T.: TL;DR: cross-region failover + kernel mismatch + microbatch singletons -> KV thrash -> tail blowup. Short-term: rollback (done). Medium-term: kernel-aware routing + affinity + microbatch guardrails. Adding @platform-eng to follow up. :mag:
